text:
maya: FYI hitting a weird edge with the Python SDK -> internal proxy path. route header sometimes not making it through, which results in console quota attribution showing an empty route for some requests.

sam: ugh. repro steps?

maya: minimal: app uses sdk v2.14.1, we set route via client.set_route('paywall') before calling generate. interal proxy shows no x-rd-route on some requests. happens around cold starts and when we import our internal proxy shim early.

leo: could be init ordering race. we saw similar with session-affinity where the shim registers after the auth plugin.

maya: I added logging in the SDK and it looks like when the shim mutates the request object in our startup hook, the header gets lost during the internal proxy's request clone.

anna: do we have telemetry traces for those requests? trace-id correlation might help narrow whether headers dropped client-side or server-side.

maya: infra-bot: traced span attached: https://console.internal/traces/6832 (mock link)

infra-bot: Reaction :eyes: (automated)

sam: quick idea: in SDK we currently add route header in Client._prepare_request. if user code or a shim copies/rewrites the Request object later, that header can disappear. maybe move route header into transport layer (right before send) to ensure propagation.

leo: moving to transport sounds right but could be a breaking change for some internal shims that expect header in Request earlier. need compatibility check.

maya: agreed. we should avoid breaking users. maybe make it opt-in via env var or feature flag while we roll out. default to keep current behavior for this minor release, then flip in a patch release after canary.

anna: console folks will want consistent telemetry. If header moves later, our console ingestion needs to look at the outgoing wire header, not the Request object. telemetry mapping change needed.

sam: patch proposal: introduce CLIENT_ROUTE_METADATA_PHASE=post_prepare which moves header injection to transport when enabled. add unit tests covering shim-copy scenarios and an integration test with the internal proxy image to validate header on the wire.

maya: will open PR with tests + a migration note in changelog. also instrument SDK to emit an event when header added so console can ingest that signal if needed.

leo: please include a clear rollout plan: opt-in, 1-week canary on internal teams, then 2-week gradual enable for larger customers. we should add a console flag to surface when SDKs are in the new mode for a tenant.

anna: console implementation notes: we can add a boolean column "sdk_injected_route" in request ingestion and a dashboard tile showing percent of requests with missing route vs sdk_injected_route. that helps correlate.

sam: followups: (1) PR with code + tests (maya) (2) console schema change (anna) (3) infra proxy integration test update (leo) (4) docs + changelog (maya).

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/6832 (draft). will add changelog and migration section.

leo: devex ask: add a short snippet to the Python quickstart showing how to opt into the new env var so customers can test. also add a note on deprecation timeline if we plan to flip default.

maya: noted. timeline proposal: opt-in for 2 weeks, then opt-out window of 30 days, then flip default in next minor. we should communicate via console banner and release notes.

anna: QA: create a small dashboard alert that fires if >0.5% of requests have empty route for a tenant during the canary; route leakage should be near zero.

sam: one more concern: Go/TS SDKs. if Python changes behavior we need alignment across clients. can we do the same transport-layer injection pattern there?

leo: yes, but implementers beware of language differences in Request copying semantics. I'll sync with Go/TS leads.

maya: thanks. I'll queue the PR and post updates. will tag @sam @leo @anna on the PR.

sam: thanks, maya. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: sdk-route-transport-change/6832.

maya: last note: include a small migration test script for customers that spins up the proxy locally and validates header presence (we can add to devex repo).

leo: love it. keep updates here and we'll plan a quick sync before canary.
